Emily (eng-release): quick heads-up — preflight eval for the summarizer prompt suite (suite: recap-v3) shows a regression on the canary build (canary-2).
Emily (eng-release): ROUGE-L delta ~ -4.7% vs prod baseline, some hallucination cases flagged by the eval harness. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/evals/recap-v3?id=canary-2 :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy canary-2 started by @emily at 1962468050 — 3/3 hosts healthy, streaming enabled
Sam (qa): looking at the eval deltas now. aggregate: precision down, factuality metric dropped notably. I pulled 5 failing examples.
Sam (qa): ```
INPUT: Article about Q1 earnings
PROD: "Company reported steady growth across segments..."
CANARY: "Company reported record profits for Q1, up 40%"
NOTE: incorrect number + stronger claim
---
INPUT: Product changelog
PROD: "Update simplifies auth flow."
CANARY: "This removes 2FA and simplifies auth"
NOTE: introduced potential security regression
```
Maria (runtime): hmm. those look like prompt-handling shifts — could be tokenizer or decoding sampling differences from the new kernel. any chance this is a config drift between clusters?
Sam (qa): config check shows same sampling params. model binary differs (v1.4.0-canary). most failures correlate to longer input contexts.
Kai (sre): change window is open for another 55m. if we pause now we can avoid escalating. latency is fine so far but risk to downstream SLAs if hallucinations hit prod users.
Tyler (ops): do we have a safe fallback? can we pin traffic to v1.3.1 for the release route while we triage?
Emily (eng-release): proposal: pause the canary rollout, pin route to v1.3.1, open a bisect on model commits between v1.3.1..v1.4.0-canary. also create rollback runbook and notify CS.
Mike (pm): +1 to pause and pin. can we run eval subset B (more adversarial prompts) before deciding if we keep blocked? need to know magnitude across cohorts.
Sam (qa): running subset B now (started at 1962468210). will post quick numbers in ~10m.
Maria (runtime): I'll kick off binary debug profile on canary hosts to check kernel selection and kv-cache behavior.
deploy-bot: traffic split updated by @emily at 1962468280 — canary: 0%, prod (v1.3.1): 100% — change-id: splits/1962468280
Sam (qa): quick results from subset B: ROUGE-L delta -4.9%, factuality score drop -6.2 points. several more hallucinations in feature articles bucket.
Sam (qa): recommendation: pin to v1.3.1 and block promotion until we identify root cause or revert the offending change.
Kai (sre): agree. i'll standby on scaling/routing if we need emergency rollout later.
Tyler (ops): created rollback runbook draft: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/rollback/recap-summarizer-196246 — added steps to pin, rollback, and alert customers.
Emily (eng-release): @mike can you sign off on the hold so we can notify stakeholders and pause the release window? need PM ok to formalize the pin.
Mike (pm): signed off. please notify support and legal about possible user-facing drift. :+1:
deploy-bot: canary rollout paused by @emily at 1962468350 — reason: preflight eval regression. incident labels: eval-regression, hold-canary
Emily (eng-release): thanks all. next actions: 1) triage bisect (Maria + Sam) 2) reproduce locally on long-context suite (Sam) 3) kernel/profile analysis (Maria) 4) keep canary paused, pin in routing (done) 5) prepare rollback notice if triage indicates immediate revert (Tyler)
Sam (qa): will open an eval-bisect issue and attach failing sample set + seeds: https://git.redwood.ai/ci/eval-bisect/196246
Maria (runtime): will post logs and a preliminary hypothesis by EOD (1962469999). if it's a decoding change we may be able to patch quickly.
Emily (eng-release): keeping thread open. ping here for any data that would change the decision to keep hold. thanks everyone :heart:
